# DAY MILE

## Campaign
- Brand name: DAY MILE
- Campaign line: Your city. Your pace.
- Audience: ordinary urban runners
- Activities: preparation, easy running, recovery
- Existing mark: black dynamic stroke in logo.png

## Product
- Product: one running-shoe model, shown as a matching pair
- Upper colour: off-white #F4F1EA
- Sole accent colour: orange #FF5A1F
- Side-view identity: shoe-1.png
- Top-view identity: shoe-2.png
- Three-quarter-view identity: shoe-3.png

## Casting
| Runner | Identity source | Wardrobe | Campaign status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Morgan Reed | morgan-reed.png | Sage #798777 crew-neck T-shirt, charcoal #303236 running shorts, white ankle socks | Approved campaign subject |

## Morgan Reed

- Appearance: medium-brown skin, short tightly curled dark hair, clean-shaven face, average build

- Shooting area: 12000 mm east-west by 8000 mm north-south

- Protected advertising content: face, both shoes, brand name, campaign line, existing mark

steps.userMessage:
DAY MILE | Running shoes for the hours around a run

We are launching DAY MILE to people who fit running around work, errands and the journey home. Build a photography campaign around the same running-shoe model worn by Alex Lane and Morgan Reed in everyday city settings. The shoe has an off-white #F4F1EA upper and an orange #FF5A1F sole accent; its construction and markings follow the three attached shoe views. Use the existing black stroke mark from logo.png. Print "DAY MILE" and "Your city. Your pace." on the advertising images and video end frame.

Alex's appearance and outfit follow alex-lane.png. Morgan's appearance and outfit follow morgan-reed.png. Photograph preparation, easy running and recovery in the first 60 minutes after sunrise. The shared lighting treatment is southeast sunlight at approximately 20 degrees elevation, a 4:1 key-to-fill ratio and 5200 K white balance. The finished campaign uses landscape 3:2, square 1:1 and vertical 9:16 compositions. Advertising copy sits within the upper quarter; faces, both shoes and copy remain inside an 8% inset from every edge. In whole-product photographs, the pair spans at least 80% of the image width.

Audience: ordinary urban runners considering their next everyday running shoe, with our brand and media teams selecting the launch imagery and placements.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the product, casting, lighting and copy facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. shoe-1.png is the identity reference for the shoe's side view. shoe-2.png is the identity reference for its top view. shoe-3.png is the identity reference for its three-quarter view. logo.png supplies the existing identity mark. alex-lane.png supplies Alex Lane's identity and wardrobe. morgan-reed.png supplies Morgan Reed's identity and wardrobe. campaign-safe-zones.png defines the carrier constraints for the three advertising proportions. morning-light-plan.png defines the lighting positions within a 12000 mm by 8000 mm shooting area. dawn-street.png supplies an empty-location reference for morning light and street surfaces.

Deliverables:
1. Three distinct shooting-concept boards, one each for directions A, B and C, comparing the runner's action, camera position and relationship to the city
2. One selected-concept shooting sheet naming A, B or C and its selection rationale, with a shot list recording shot IDs, proportions, camera positions, subjects and uses, plus the shoe colours, lighting treatment and copy
3. Seven finished runner photographs: S01, Alex Lane warming up on a pavement; S02, Morgan Reed climbing station steps; S03, Alex running beside a canal; S04, Morgan running beside the canal; S05, Alex recovering outside the station; S06, Morgan tying laces on the pavement; S07, Alex pausing by a shopfront; S01 and S06 as landscape campaign images with the existing mark and both copy lines
4. Three whole-product heroes of the pair on pavement: P01, three-quarter view; P02, top view; P03, side view
5. Four product close-ups: D01, the mesh-to-sole junction; D02, the lacing and tongue; D03, the heel construction; D04, the toe mesh
6. Four advertising crops, square and vertical versions of both S01 and S06, with the existing mark and both copy lines
7. One 10-second advertising video moving from Alex's preparation to Morgan's run and a product end frame
8. One campaign presentation of at least 12 pages, reusing the three concepts, selected shooting sheet, all finished photographs, all advertising crops and video stills, with an ordered image sequence

Acceptance:
- Concept boards A, B and C precede the shooting sheet; the sheet selects one by letter, and all seven runner photographs, three product heroes, four close-ups, four advertising crops and the video develop that selection. The presentation names the same letter on page 1.
- The shooting sheet records #F4F1EA, #FF5A1F, southeast light at approximately 20 degrees, the first 60 minutes after sunrise, 4:1 key-to-fill and 5200 K; the presentation repeats these facts beside the relevant finished images, and its sequence captions repeat the sheet's shot IDs and proportions.
- S01–S07 and the video preserve Alex's and Morgan's respective reference appearances and clothing; every visible shoe in the photographs, advertising crops and video retains the model's reference construction, colours and markings.
- P01–P03 each show the complete pair spanning at least 80% of the image width in the three named views; D01–D04 each resolve their named construction detail.
- S01 and its two advertising crops share one exposure, and S06 and its two crops share another, each at 3:2, 1:1 and 9:16; all six images carry DAY MILE, Your city. Your pace. and the existing black mark, with copy in the upper quarter and faces, both shoes and copy inside the 8% edge inset.
- The 10-second video ends with the existing mark and both copy lines; the presentation contains at least 12 pages, reproduces all 18 finished still images and orders them as preparation, running, recovery and product.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
